projectBackground.name: Statutory Audit — Brightwell Distribution
projectBackground.timeline: Fieldwork in two weeks, sign-off in five
projectBackground.context: Brightwell's revenue grew 30% with a thin finance team. The engagement partner expects controls testing and fraud-risk consideration.

manager.name: Tom Whitfield
manager.note: The file has to speak for itself. Anyone reading it a year from now should see what you tested, what you found and why you concluded as you did.

assignment.title: Plan, test and conclude on the Brightwell audit
assignment.brief: Calculate materiality and sample interval, evaluate evidence quality and fraud flags, run a controls test in Excel and draft one management letter finding.

documents.name: Controls Walkthrough Notes
documents.note: Purchase approvals, payroll and cash receipts; the same clerk raises and approves some invoices.

documents.name: Journal Entry Listing
documents.note: Several large round-sum manual entries posted on the last day of the year.

tasks.title: Quality of Evidence
tasks.prompt: Which audit evidence is generally most reliable?
options: A bank confirmation obtained directly by the auditor from the bank
A copy of a statement provided by the client
tasks.reasoning: External evidence obtained directly by the auditor is more reliable than internal or oral evidence.
tasks.tip: Source, independence and directness all raise reliability.
tasks.mistake: Relying on client-provided copies allows alteration to go unnoticed.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Performance Materiality
tasks.prompt: Overall materiality is 0.5% of revenue of £12,500,000. Performance materiality is set at 75% of overall materiality. What is performance materiality?
tasks.reasoning: Performance materiality is set below overall materiality so misstatements in aggregate stay below it.
tasks.tip: Calculate overall materiality first, then apply the percentage.
tasks.mistake: Using overall materiality for testing risks missing small errors that add up.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Sampling Interval
tasks.prompt: Monetary unit sampling: population £3,600,000 and sample size 60. What is the sampling interval?
tasks.reasoning: The interval is the population value divided by the number of items selected.
tasks.tip: Select every Nth monetary unit starting from a random point.
tasks.mistake: Confusing interval with sample size gives the wrong selection.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Segregation of Duties
tasks.prompt: One clerk raises purchase invoices and also approves them for payment. This is:
options: Only an issue if invoices are large
A segregation-of-duties weakness that increases fraud and error risk
tasks.reasoning: Duties must be separated so one person cannot both initiate and approve a transaction.
tasks.tip: Look for who can start, approve and record a transaction.
tasks.mistake: Treating it as acceptable ignores a classic fraud pathway.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Fraud Risk Indicators
tasks.prompt: Select the indicators that raise fraud risk.
options: Large round-sum manual journals on the last day of the year
Pressure to hit a bonus target
tasks.reasoning: Unusual manual journals, override and incentive are standard fraud-triangle indicators.
tasks.tip: Pair opportunity with pressure and rationalisation.
tasks.mistake: Missing these signals leaves the highest-risk area untested.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Controls Test (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Calculate the deviation rate (%) = Exceptions / Sample x 100 in column D for each control. Upload for checking.
tasks.reasoning: The deviation rate compares exceptions to the sample so you can judge whether a control can be relied on.
tasks.tip: Compare the rate to the tolerable rate set in planning.
tasks.mistake: Counting exceptions without the sample size cannot support a conclusion.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Management Letter Point
tasks.prompt: Draft a 3-4 sentence management letter finding on the segregation-of-duties weakness.
tasks.modelAnswer: We noted that one finance clerk both raises and approves supplier invoices, so no independent review prevents erroneous or fraudulent payments. Because Brightwell's purchases have grown significantly, the risk has increased. We recommend assigning approval to a different employee or introducing a system-enforced two-step approval, and an independent monthly review of payments. We will re-test this control at the next audit.
tasks.reasoning: A good finding states the condition, risk, recommendation and follow-up.
tasks.mistake: Vague findings without a recommendation are not actionable.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Journal That Wasn't Reviewed
caseStudy.background: A distribution company's finance manager posted unsupported year-end journals that inflated revenue by £310,000. The audit team had sampled invoices but never tested manual journals.
caseStudy.challenges: Audit work concentrated on routine transactions; manual entries were not tested.
caseStudy.constraints: Management override is hard to detect without targeted procedures.
questions: Why are manual journals a fraud risk?
Which audit procedure would have found it?
How should auditors respond to override risk?
caseStudy.solution: Ledger & Co. made journal entry testing a mandatory procedure on every audit, including unusual timing and round sums.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Always test management override; fraud hides where nobody looks.

options: One person controlling a whole transaction
